text:
maria: Heads-up — after the telemetry sampler tweak yesterday I'm seeing repeated frame drops and slow heatmap tiles on EU canary. Charts take ~350-500ms longer to first-paint. Seems correlated with a bunch of cold tile/network requests. @liam any idea?

liam: :eyes: can you paste a small HAR or the network waterfall? also which bundle/commit on canary?

maria: Canary is `console-canary@2026-03-19-telemetry-sampler-v2` (deploy msg below). Attached small waterfall — most of the extra time is on `GET /tile` miss then an extra parse/rehydrate.

maria: ```
Requests: tile1 200ms -> parse 120ms
         tile2 220ms -> parse 140ms
Bundle: main.chunk.js (+120kb)
Devtools summary: CPU spikes around k-v cache miss handlers (client cache warmup)
```

ash: Noted. The sampler change reduced telemetry emission from clients to 10eps and we also changed prefetch signal to only run when `telemetry.sampled === true`. That coupling was intended to reduce backend noise but it might be starving the client-side prefetch predictor of signals.

jonah: SRE checked infra — no region-wide regression. Host latencies stable. The timing aligns exactly with the canary deploy of `telemetry-sampler-v2`.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-19T18:22:11 - console-canary/telemetry-sampler-v2 -> eu-canary

liam: OK so hypothesis: adaptive prefetch window uses recent telemetry hits to predict which tiles to warm. With sampling reduced, predictor thinks traffic is cold and shrinks `prefetch_window_ms`, leading to more cold misses and parse overhead.

maria: That matches what I see. Quick experiment: I bumped `prefetch_window_ms: 200 -> 600` in the console client locally and the heatmap time-to-interactive improved ~280ms.

liam: Could be two mitigations: (A) decouple the predictor from raw telemetry sampling (use synthetic or heuristics for cold detection) or (B) fall back to server-side prefetch when client-sampled-rate < 0.3. Prefer A long-term.

ash: Sketching a short patch for A — an exponential backoff on window shrink that requires at least N consecutive low-sample ticks before reducing below baseline. Here's a config sketch:```json
{
  "prefetch": {
    "baseline_window_ms": 400,
    "min_window_ms": 150,
    "shrink_threshold_ticks": 5,
    "backoff_factor": 0.8
  }
}
```

maria: Nice. Also propose we emit a small internal metric `prefetch_misfire` whenever a tile request had no cache hint and the predictor predicted low affinity — add to console telemetry so we can alert on canaries.

jonah: +1, add a burn-in alert: if prefetch_misfire_rate > 0.05 for 5m on canary, auto-rollback. SRE can wire that into the rollout pipeline.

liam: Short-term hotfix: revert the change that gated prefetch on `telemetry.sampled` only for canary (10m hotfix). I can open PR and fast-roll it.

maria: Please. If we revert, I'll run the same synthetic traces and attach before/after HAR + flamegraphs.

liam: PR opened: #4021 — revert telemetry gating on prefetch for canary. Requesting quick review. :thumbsup:

ash: Deployed revert to canary 10m ago — early signals look promising, chart first-paint improved ~230ms on the same synthetic run. We'll keep adaptive window patch as a follow-up.

maria: Confirming canary looks stable now. I'll start A/B plan for `prefetch_mode: fixed|adaptive` with a 2% progressive rollout and `prefetch_misfire` alerting enabled.

jonah: Also run a short regression suite against the console synthetic harness (tile-heavy trace) for both EU & US. I can schedule that.

maria: Thanks all. Follow-ups: PR #4021 (revert), issue #789 (adaptive prefetch heuristics), playbook update for telemetry-rollouts. Dropping the HAR and flamegraph in the thread: https://redwood-internal/share/har-heatmap-2026-03-19.zip

sre-bot: Regression run queued: console-tile-synthetic (eu, us) — results expected in ~45m

liam: TL;DR: telemetry sampling change inadvertently starved client predictor -> smaller prefetch windows -> more cold loads -> chart slowness. Hotfix reverted on canary; follow-up adaptive heuristic + metric planned.
